title: Affordable housing plan for 2025 University Ave E
subtitle: Town Square parking expropriation, infrastructure funding, asset management plan tabled, AMO board nomination, and extreme heat planning request.
overview: Council endorsed a vision for affordable and attainable housing on city-owned land at 2025 University Ave E and directed staff to request a Ministerial Zoning Order from the province {{vote:m7}}. The site is currently zoned for employment use. The plan now includes some commercial space, which residents asked for during consultation, and the draft zoning allows up to 12 storeys, with lower heights on the northern part of the site. Staff expect to issue a request for proposals to non-profit builders this summer, with a recommendation to Council in December.

Council also authorized expropriation proceedings for land at the Waterloo Town Square north parking lot {{vote:m6}} and approved an infrastructure replacement plan for 2024 to 2026 that includes road resurfacing and sewer repairs {{vote:m8}}. The 2024 Asset Management Plan was tabled, with a decision set for June 17, 2024 {{vote:m4}}. Council received the 2023 wastewater and stormwater annual reports {{vote:m5}}.

Council supported the mayor's nomination to the AMO Board of Directors {{vote:m9}}. The meeting began with a closed session on legal and land matters. The minutes report no decisions from it. Staff will look into a city-wide approach to extreme heat.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed the proposed vision and draft zoning and directed staff to request a Ministerial Zoning Order, with progress updates posted on Engage Waterloo.

decisions.item: Waterloo Town Square north parking lot
decisions.detail: Council authorized the City Solicitor to begin expropriation proceedings for the identified lands, for the municipal purposes set out in the report.

Council approved the 2024-2026 implementation plan, released 2024 capital funding, approved 2026 funding subject to budget confirmation, and reallocated money between road resurfacing and sewer repair projects.
Council received the report as information and set June 17, 2024 for a decision.
Council received the annual wastewater collection and stormwater management reports and approved the related staff report.
Council supported the mayor's nomination to the AMO Board for the Large Urban Caucus position and directed the City Clerk to prepare a support letter.

debate: Councillors welcomed the changes made after consultation, including added commercial space and more height, and said the process showed how concerns would be addressed later, such as traffic through a traffic impact study.

Residents near the site raised concerns about well water. Staff said wells would be monitored before and during construction, and that municipal water services are available nearby if connection is needed.
A delegate from a housing co-operative supported the plan. The delegate urged keeping units affordable permanently and cautioned against favouring land leases, because they can complicate financing.

A resident delegate said the provincial affordability definition, based on the 60th income percentile, is too high. The delegate asked for a lower ceiling and for concrete proposals to reduce parking. Staff said they would use that definition as the upper limit, award points for deeper affordability and work with the region on a minimum.

Councillors asked about Indigenous engagement and the province's timing. Staff said engagement would continue through the environmental study terms of reference. They also said the province's decision timeline is outside city control.
